title: Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent: A Reliability Audit of Cybersecurity LLM Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2609.08765v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) benchmarks are often treated as fixed datasets with stable scores, yet their outcomes depend on configurable evaluation pipelines. We audit eight cybersecurity benchmarks across 10 proprietary, open-weight, and cybersecurity-specialized LLMs. By modeling benchmarks as measurement pipelines, we identify 15 systematic failure modes and show that a single pipeline choice can change a model's score by more than 80 percentage points and substantially alter model rankings. At the cross-benchmark level, two semantically similar task pairs rank the same models differently because of incompatible evaluation conventions. Under an evaluation harness that standardizes pipeline choices while preserving task semantics, nine of 10 models shift by at least three ranks on at least one benchmark. These results show that cybersecurity LLM benchmark scores are pipeline-dependent and motivate pipeline-aware auditing as a core req

translated_title: 基准测试分数依赖于评估流程：网络安全大语言模型基准的可靠性审计
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）基准测试通常被视为具有稳定分数的固定数据集，然而其结果实际上取决于可配置的评估流程。我们对8个网络安全基准在10个专有、开放权重和网络安全专用大语言模型上进行了审计。通过将基准测试建模为测量流程，我们识别出15种系统性失败模式，并表明单一的流程选择可以使模型分数变化超过80个百分点，并显著改变模型排名。在跨基准层面，两个语义相似的任务对由于不兼容的评估惯例而对模型给出不同的排名。在一个在保留任务语义的同时标准化流程选择的统一评估框架下，10个模型中有9个在至少一个基准上排名变化至少三位。这些结果表明，网络安全大语言模型基准测试分数依赖于评估流程，因此需要将流程感知的审计作为核心要求。
tldr: 网络安全大语言模型基准测试的分数高度依赖于评估流程的配置——单一的流程选择可使模型分数变化超过80个百分点并显著改变排名，因此亟需采用流程感知的审计方法来保障基准评测结果的可靠性。
en_tdlr: Cybersecurity LLM benchmark scores are pipeline-dependent—a single evaluation pipeline choice can shift a model's score by over 80 percentage points and substantially alter rankings—motivating pipeline-aware auditing as a core requirement for reliable benchmarking.
